developments: Bitcoin faded through the US session to about $61,350 on Kraken at 21:35 UK, down about 2% from the afternoon edition and below Monday's $64,520 high, even as US stocks extended their gains.
The US Justice Department filed to seize about $1.17 billion in USDC linked to the Binance hack, with Circle agreeing to issue replacement tokens if a court orders forfeiture, The Block reported.
Zcash gave back most of its spike, trading near $791 on Kraken, about 6% below the afternoon edition and down slightly on the day.
briefing.changed: Softer than this afternoon. Stocks held and built on the Nvidia rally, with the Nasdaq up about 6.9% late in the session, but bitcoin slipped back towards where it started the day, so the gap between crypto and tech widened.
briefing.question: Why did bitcoin fade while stocks held? A strong dollar and a near-certain December Fed rise, or steady US-hours selling that has not yet turned?
briefing.watch: Monday's spot bitcoin ETF flow figures, due Tuesday morning UK, then US PCE inflation on Wednesday at 13:30 UK. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Bitcoin fades towards $61,000 as stocks keep rallying
lead.standfirst: Bitcoin gave back most of Monday's Nvidia-driven jump in US trading, even as the Nasdaq held a gain of almost 7%.
body: Bitcoin traded near $61,350 on Kraken at 21:35 UK, Kraken data showed, about 2% below the afternoon edition and some $3,200 under the day's high of $64,520. Bitcoin Magazine reported that it dipped to about $60,800 at 19:45 UK.

The fade came while US shares stayed strong. The Nasdaq Composite was up about 6.9% and the S&P 500 about 5% at 20:40 UK, Bitcoin Magazine reported, after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.

Bitcoin Magazine pointed to a stronger dollar, with the dollar index up about 0.65% to 104.40, keeping a December Fed rise in play. CoinDesk cited Tesseract's Adam Haeems as saying bitcoin had fallen in seven of the eight US sessions since Huang stepped down, and noted that it had recovered only about a quarter of its fall from $74,000, against more than four-fifths of Nvidia's.

Separately, the US Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint seeking about $1.17 billion in USDC tied to the Binance hack, The Block reported, with Circle agreeing to issue equivalent new tokens to the US if a court orders forfeiture.

Spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $1.79 billion last week, a fourth straight week of outflows, Bitcoin Magazine reported. Monday's flows are due on Tuesday morning UK time, ahead of October's PCE inflation data on Wednesday.

headline: Bitcoin faded to about $61,350 by the evening as the Nvidia-led stock rally held, leaving it little changed on the day. The US moved to seize $1.17 billion in USDC from the Binance hack.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, evening edition, Monday the twenty third of November. Bitcoin has drifted back to about sixty one thousand three hundred and fifty dollars, around two percent lower than this afternoon and well below the day's high near sixty four and a half thousand, even though US shares held a big rally on Nvidia's news. A stronger dollar and a likely Fed rate rise in December are being blamed. Zcash has given back its spike and sits near seven hundred and ninety dollars. The US is moving to seize over a billion dollars of stablecoins from the Binance hack. Watch ETF flows tomorrow morning and US inflation on Wednesday at half past one. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Bitcoin fades to about $61,350 as stocks hold their rally
stories.why: Kraken showed bitcoin near $61,350 at 21:35 UK, down from about $62,570 at the afternoon edition and the $64,520 high, and only slightly above its daily open. Bitcoin Magazine reported a dip to about $60,800 and $321 million of bitcoin liquidations, $224 million of them shorts. The afternoon read of bitcoin moving with tech no longer holds: stocks held their gains while bitcoin gave them back.

note.read: Bitcoin is lagging tech: CoinDesk noted it recovered about a quarter of its drop versus more than four-fifths for Nvidia, which points to crypto-specific selling rather than a pure risk-asset trade.
note.alt: The spike was mostly short covering, so the fade may simply be those positions running out rather than fresh selling.
note.change: A return of spot ETF inflows, or a hold above $64,500, would suggest the lag is closing; a break below $60,000 would point the other way.

stories.title: Dollar climbs further as a December Fed rise stays the base case
stories.why: Bitcoin Magazine reported the dollar index up about 0.65% at 104.40 and said a quarter-point rise at the 8 to 9 December Fed meeting remained the base case; CoinDesk put the two-year Treasury yield near 4.7% and said markets price a December rise as near certain. The new evidence is that the strong dollar is now being cited as the main reason bitcoin failed to hold its gains.
stories.caveat: Outlets differ on when the dollar was last this strong: Bitcoin Magazine said April 2025, CoinDesk said March 2025.

note.read: A firm dollar and rising rate expectations act as a brake on bitcoin even when equities rally.
note.alt: Bitcoin may simply be thinner and more exposed to US-hours selling than stocks, with the dollar a coincidence.
note.change: A soft PCE reading on Wednesday that cools rate-rise bets would test whether the dollar is the real driver.

stories.title: US files to seize $1.17 billion in USDC from the Binance hack
stories.why: The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint for about $1.17 billion in USDC across 36 addresses on 18 blockchains, which it attributes to North Korean hackers, The Block reported. Circle has blocked the tokens and agreed to issue equivalent new USDC to the US on a forfeiture order. Decrypt separately reported that $247 million of the hack proceeds has moved through bitcoin mixers, so frozen stablecoins limit, but do not remove, the risk of stolen funds being sold.

stories.title: Zcash gives back its spike, near $791
stories.why: Kraken showed ZEC near $791 at 21:35 UK, down about 6% from $841 at the afternoon edition and slightly below its daily open of about $798, after a range of $775 to $907. The afternoon's sharp rise has fully unwound, which fits the earlier caution that the move to $907 was thin and short-lived.
stories.caveat: No ZEC-specific news was found for either the spike or the retreat.

stories.title: ARK withdraws two planned crypto index ETFs
stories.why: ARK Invest asked the SEC to withdraw registrations for two crypto ETFs linked to the CoinDesk 20 index, filed in January, CoinDesk reported, without giving a reason. It is a small sign of fading appetite for new crypto funds after four straight weeks of spot bitcoin ETF outflows totalling about $1.79 billion last week, as Bitcoin Magazine reported.

stories.title: Miner Bitdeer sells all 281 BTC it mined last week
stories.why: Bitdeer mined and sold 281.1 BTC last week and held no bitcoin of its own as of 20 November, Bitcoin Magazine reported, down from about 2,000 BTC at the end of 2025. Miners selling their full output adds steady supply at a time when the largest corporate buyer, Strategy, bought only 457 BTC.

explained.title: Why bitcoin can lag a stock rally
body: On a risk-on day, bitcoin and tech shares often rise together. But bitcoin also has its own buyers and sellers: ETF flows, miners selling what they mine, and companies that hold it. When those are net sellers, bitcoin can fall back even while stocks keep rising.

A strong dollar adds to this. Bitcoin is priced in dollars and is sensitive to interest-rate expectations, so a firmer dollar and talk of Fed rate rises can hold it back more than they hold back a company with booming profits.

investigating: Did ETF buyers return during Monday's rally? Evidence: Monday's spot bitcoin ETF flow figures, due Tuesday morning UK.
Is US-hours selling easing? Evidence: whether bitcoin holds its level through Tuesday's US session, which Tesseract said fell in seven of the last eight.
Did Chainflip recover its stolen BTC after the 18:38 UK bounty deadline? No statement was found this evening; evidence would be a Chainflip update or on-chain movement of the 122.9 BTC.
